title: Saints must leave Babylon and prepare to meet the Bridegroom
setting: Church leaders held a conference at Hiram, Ohio, on 1–2 November 1831 to plan publishing Joseph Smith’s revelations. On 1 November Joseph dictated a revelation to serve as the book’s preface, now section 1. A later history says he dictated this one on 3 November, after elders asked about preaching and gathering. One early copy is dated 2 November, but the Joseph Smith Papers editors favor Whitmer’s 3 November copy. It came to be called the appendix. It was first printed in 1833, but not in the Book of Commandments, whose printing was stopped by violence in Missouri.
summary: The Lord’s voice calls on the Church to hear, for he will suddenly come to his temple in judgment. It tells the Saints to prepare, sanctify themselves, and gather to Zion, leaving Babylon behind. Elders are to go to all nations, first the Gentiles and then the Jews. Gentiles are to flee to Zion and Judah to Jerusalem, but not in haste. The revelation describes the Lord’s coming: lands joined, those in the north countries returning, and the saints rising from their graves. It pictures Christ in red garments, having “trodden the wine-press alone,” while his redeemed speak of his loving kindness. The Lord sent the gospel in plainness so the weak could prepare, and these commandments now go to all. Those who will not hear face darkness, because they rejected his servants.

contextNote.title: Babylon as a condition, not a city
contextNote.text: According to a later history, elders asked how the Saints should gather and preach. Verse 14 defines what they are leaving: “spiritual Babylon”. It locates Babylon in “the midst of wickedness,” not on a map. Verse 5 pairs the departure with a demand: “Be ye clean”. Verse 15 sets the pace: “let not your flight be in haste,” with all things prepared first. Verse 19 gives the purpose of leaving: to go out and meet the Bridegroom. In this passage, going out of Babylon means separating from wickedness while preparing for Christ.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 133–134 reads verses 4–14 as Christ’s call to reject Babylon and come to Zion. In verses 5 and 14, what does leaving Babylon require, and how does verse 15 caution the Saints?

newPlaces.name: Jerusalem
newPlaces.why: vv. 13, 21, 24; named as the gathering place for Judah and a place from which the Lord will speak; v. 20 also names the Mount of Olivet

reviewNote: Read all 74 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, Ohio, 3 November 1831, in answer to elders’ questions on preaching and gathering, and notes it was first an appendix. JSP historical introduction read: conference of 1–2 November on publishing the revelations; preface dictated 1 November; Sidney Rigdon’s copy endorsed 2 November and called ‘An appendix’; John Whitmer’s copy dated 3 November is preferred; first published May 1833 in The Evening and the Morning Star; labeled appendix in 1835 D&C. The occasion rests on a later history, not the conference minutes. Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and ‘John’ (v. 55) are named but not added; Zion, Babylon, and Mount Zion treated as figurative. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary corrected: in v. 52 the redeemed mention the Lord's loving kindness (the Lord does not 'recall his people'); Christ's appearance now attributed to the text's picture.
